History & Physical (Detailed)

Consult Summary:
48-year-old man with 3-day history of watery diarrhea (5–6×/day) following brief vomiting, now weak and mildly dehydrated; telehealth assessment consistent with acute self-limiting gastroenteritis.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Watery, loose stools for 3 days.  
• Onset/Timeline: Began suddenly 3 days ago with two episodes of vomiting; vomiting resolved, diarrhea persists.  
• Frequency/severity: 5–6 bowel movements/day, described as “very bad,” watery.  
• Associated symptoms: Feels very dehydrated, weak, poor appetite. Felt slightly febrile at onset but afebrile now.  
• Pertinent negatives: No visible blood in stool, no abdominal pain, no headache, no myalgias.  
• Exacerbants/relievers: None identified; attempts oral fluids but feels they “go straight through.”

Past Medical History:
• Asthma – mild/intermittent; uses short-acting β-agonist inhaler as needed; no recent exacerbations.

Medications:
• Salbutamol (blue) inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
Allergies: Denies known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives alone; software engineer.  
• Smoking: Never.  
• Alcohol: Infrequent/social use.  
• Recently off work for 3 days due to illness.

Family History:
• Father: Hypertension; deceased (bowel cancer at age unspecified).  
• Mother: Type 2 diabetes.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not recorded (telemedicine visit).  
• General/abdomen/other systems: Not recorded.

Investigations:
• None performed or ordered at this visit.

Assessment & Plan:
Overall Impression:
Acute infectious gastroenteritis with mild dehydration; currently appears suitable for outpatient management.

DDx Integration (brief):
1. Gastroenteritis – watery diarrhea, preceding vomiting, self-limited course; no red-flag features.  
2. Dehydration – subjective dryness/weakness; no objective vitals to grade severity.

Issue 1: Acute gastroenteritis ± mild dehydration  
Plan:  
• Oral rehydration therapy – advise OTC oral rehydration salts (e.g., Dioralyte).  
• Encourage clear fluids, small sips frequently; resume light diet as tolerated.  
• Symptomatic relief: Paracetamol for malaise/fever (dose not discussed; patient to follow package instructions).  
• Work exclusion: Remain off work until ≥24–48 h diarrhea-free.  
• Red-flag safety net: Seek urgent care for persistent vomiting, inability to keep fluids down, blood in stool, high fever, severe abdominal pain, or worsening weakness.  
• Follow-up: Re-evaluate next week if symptoms not improved or sooner if red-flag symptoms develop.

Issue 2: Asthma – stable  
Plan: Continue salbutamol inhaler as needed; no change required today.

General plan items:
• No routine labs/imaging indicated at this stage.  
• Encourage rest, adequate nutrition once appetite returns.

Quality checks:
• Missing vitals and physical exam data – limitation of telehealth setting.  
• Medications list may be incomplete; only inhaler discussed.  
• No documented drug allergies but patient denies any.  
• Transcript quality adequate; no conflicting data between transcript and DDx.
